# Chapter Eight: The Tower

> *"The box was unsealed, and evil poured forth into the world, but with that evil was born a seed, that seed grew into a great tree sheltering man from that evil, that tree was named hope."*
> — **Book of Aurtus**

He held the small piece of cotton parchment between his fingers watching as it practically glowed as Juric Rogan held it up close to the lantern light, the familiar scrawl barely present this close to the light, pulling it back, pictures resolved, laying out a path to the answers that would change his life.

The location of the tower, he thought, studying it carefully as he moved it closer and then further from the small lamp that sat upon the large mahogany desk in his office.

I should be happy, triumphant he thought Juric couldn’t shake the doubt and fear that nibbled at the edges of his mind as he continued to study the parchment, since he had been turned onto this by the spymaster many people had warned him against finding out what went on there. People he feared and respected told him he would be better off not finding out, that finding this place, unlocking the secrets would change him forever.

He sat deliberating this, his eyes boring into the small piece of paper as if boring into it, as if beneath the mundane ink the secrets of the tower would reveal themselves, that somehow the innocent scrawl would transform, telling him something of the intent of this black tower.

Rogan picked up a simple beaten looking wooden ball its white paint worn and chipped. The ball belonged to ancient game still played by small children, something named after an insect he recalled, a memory floated to the surface of hitting the white ball with a mallet through wooden hoops in the ground, something he had done at a very young age, one of the magical times he had spent in the garden with his empress.

Rogan shook it off, the memory fading, taking the ball he threw it at the large wooden door, leaving an indent in the wood to accompany the hundreds of others currently littering the surface.

A moment later Loric, poked his head in, his young earnest faced assistant would have looked more at home on a farm then in an office, but the young man had a head for numbers that bordered on the supernatural Rogan thought motioning towards the ball as the young man came in and with practiced ease, scooped it up and tossed it back to his boss.

“What can I do for you my Lord?” he said, doing his best to keep the annoyance out of his voice. Rogan suppressed a smile. “Have my horse supplied and saddled. I am leaving for a few days, if anyone asks, I am on a fact-finding mission in the north,” he finished.

Loric waited his eyebrow arched with curiosity but soon he stepped back towards the door when he realized that was all he was going to get out of his boss. “Of course, my lord. The empress is traveling, so you’re not needed right now. I’ll ensure it’s done,” he said.

Leaving the room as Rogan turned towards the window, losing himself in the thoughts of the simple game’s children play as he tossed the ball into the air, catching it easily and then repeating the action.

He had received the missive that morning that the Empress would be traveling to visit the armory, touring the new weaponry and manufacturing plant. His Empress was gearing up for war, with the emperor dead, things were in flux, she was now taking control of more and more of the duties the emperor had left to the lords he thought. Rogan left his office without so much as a word, a worn leather pack over his shoulder he made his way the royal stables, entering the chancellor flipped the dirty young stable boy a silverling “My horse if you please” he ordered.

The child smiled up showing off the last two of his yellowing teeth as the young Lord quickly mounted the steed and galloped out of the stables and along the market road kicking up mud as pedestrians did their best to avoid the wake, riding towards the gate of the Capital Village he looked up at the new clock tower and guard post that had been commissioned mere months before, since the Emperor’s death a lot of construction had begun in earnest to shore up the defenses in the capital.

He smiled up at the construction knowing his role in it was a crucial one. A large shadow fell over his face blocking out the sun and Rogan looked to the sky as a larger than usual airship moved overhead. His eyes followed the underside of the vessel as it lumbered under its full cargo load moving off towards the large sky dock at the edge of the capital, he caught the rectangular profile of the old cargo hauler as he noticed the

territorial flag of Dever hanging over the rear of the vessel.

It was not uncommon to see Lusor and Dever ships entering the capital despite the tension between all three nations, there was very little that could fully stop commerce as goods from each of the countries still came in almost daily.

He caught the large blue crystal shields mounted on the rear as they flared, giving the ship a boost of speed beyond just the sails, as it moved out of the way of a clipper flying military colors that continued to patrol, paying the cargo ship very little interest.

Rogan continued to stare at the floating vessels, seeming to defy gravity above him. He had studied the science behind it, knew that each ship held a large crystal secured in the center of the vessel allowing them to lift into the air, combined with the power crystals along the edges to stabilize it, giving the large ships the ability to move with versatility through the open air. The size of the crystals would dictate the speed and maneuverability of the ship.

He had seen the aftermath of what happened when you moved a ship too suddenly or the anchors on the main crystal failed.

Ripping it from the ship, the crystal would continue to float but the ship would not, it instead would come crashing to the ground he recalled a few such scenes with a shudder. The smaller guard vessel turned making another leg of their patrol route.

Clippers were a stable of the capital, used by not only the city but by privateers sanctioned by the Empress, they were a smaller ship, but had the ability to hold a larger main crystal for its size thus making it fast and light, they held a decent armament of medium and small cannons, built to overtake larger ships they could quickly disable and board an average-sized cargo vessel and as long as a larger man o’ war didn’t arrive they were the predator of the skies. These were the pride of Vicor’s defense.

He brought his horse to a stop admiring the sleek lines and carved dragon that ran the length of the ship, the head extending out beyond the bow. As a child he had held a secret love affair with the vessels and often thought of running away to join a crew. In his mind he used it as an escape while under the thumb of his overbearing father.

Rogan had survived that time, dreaming up exciting adventures aboard such ships as the one that passed overhead.

The only problem with airship travel is you really needed a dock to properly park the ship making it inconvenient for regular travel except to other larger cities.

There was still the pirate problem as well, too often cargo ships would come under attack or go missing in the northern mountains or the eastern deserts never to be seen again.

Despite the number of patrols they sent, the brigands still seem to stay one step ahead.

With a resigned sigh he forced his eyes down and his mind to the task at hand. His daydreaming would have to wait he thought with a pang of regret.

Wincing as the cold morning air bit at his skin forcing him to pull the large black fur coat closer against his skin. Rogan did his best to hide his face within the edges of the soft fur as he pushed the horse faster.

Moving towards the west and hopefully towards the answers he desperately sought.

As the sun began to warm the air, he could imagine spring was in a hard fight to replace winter, buds of green beginning to show on the surrounding trees as he passed.

The countryside was quiet giving him time to reflect. Something had been building in the kingdom for the past few years, more secrets kept, the number of political assassinations he had been asked to carry out had nearly doubled as of two years ago.

His empress was preparing for more than just mere war, a change he remembered her saying, As they spent hours in her private study, the Empress regaling him with the plan of unification, bringing the world under her rule, protecting them from a danger that was coming, was that what she was now preparing for he wondered, clearing the advisors and the nobility of the doubting elders that had always stood in the way of progress and her vision.

Rogan went back to those nights in his mind as his Empress stood, taller than life as the warm firelight framed her face, the shadows playing over her body, as she spoke” My little lord, we are a fractured people, a lost people, the old enemy, the death machine is still among us, sleeping but waiting as we fight amongst each other, our bravest and strongest die on the fields in useless wars for territory, but this will end, I will bring all the lands under my rule and from there, we will save our kind from the one that tried to destroy us” she stated her eyes bright with the fire of excitement.

She had shown him the row upon row of books written by those of the first tribe. Some of the things in those books were fantastic, he didn’t think they were even possible, but she had assured him they at one time existed.

The flying machines powered by flame instead of crystals, large iron ships that floated upon the water, the machines that thought for themselves, serving man to build the things people needed, never needing to rest or to take a break as they churned out item after item.

As she opened book after book her face became somber and her tone grew grave “Little Lord, mankind exhumed its own destruction from deep within the ice, not knowing what it was, they brought it back to civilization, it activated, in an effort to save mankind, they sent many people to the stars to sleep until it was once again safe, these my little lord were our ancients, our first men” she finished

Rogan read on through the old and dusty tomes he read the accounts from the first as they returned to an earth that held no evidence of the existence of their friends and family, of their race, he could feel the anguish as they tried to relearn how to survive off of the land, all the knowledge of the first age had been poured into the tomes that now sat upon the shelves in the Empress’s vault.

She had said there were more, and she would find them, but she had enough to try and reignite the first age of man. If the demons who invented the death machine ever returned the Empress wanted to give us a chance, he thought smiling. Everything she did, she did to save everyone.

It was the one truth that kept Rogan moving forward, it was how he could stomach the things he had to do in order to ensure her vision. He killed to save humanity and he could continue to do so he resolved. He would do whatever it took to ensure the Empress could bring about the salvation of mankind.

Rogan continued to ride, passing the small farms, watching as the simple peasants went about their day ensuring the survival of the family. Upon passing one particular farm he caught sight of the large mountain lion strung by its feet from the tree in the front yard, two young boys stood there beginning to skin the carcass when Rogan stopped.

“What happened here?” he asked, eyeing the creature about the size of his own horse, the snow-white fur of the animal was stained with the mud and blood of a fight and he could see the slashes over its midsection and back, not made by the dressing of the large animal.

The taller of the two boys stepped towards him, his dark brown eyes eyeing the Lord suspiciously.

Rogan looked him over, his caramel skin covered in perspiration as he came close, but not too close, the knife he had been using down at his side but definitely not slack in his hand he noticed.

“The cat was hunting the cows, we finally caught up with it, it put up a fight but we finally got the best of it” he said, his eyes roving over Rogan’s clothing and horse, the young man was trying to decide if Rogan was the law or simply a curious rider.

“We were within our right. It took out four cows before we brought it down,” he stated, his eyes meeting the Lords with just a hint of the defiance this boy must feel looking at a pampered lord. Well Rogan thought, I guess they figured me for the law.

The young man had cited the law, no animal could be hunted for sport without the permission of the Lord of the land, unless that animal posed a clear and present threat, he thought he knew well, it was one a lot of farmers fell ill of. He nodded at the young man smiling and motioning towards the large cat.

“What do you plan to do with it?” he asked curiously. Rogan had no issue with the boys killing the best, or any predatory species that considered human’s food for that matter.

It was not uncommon for them to come down from the woods and hunt, but the coloring on the cat was not common and looked more at home up north than here in the western dominance.

By this time the second young man, the shorter one but close enough in appearance that Rogan took them for brothers became interested in the conversation, stepping up next to his brother.

“We were thinking of selling the pelt and smoking the meat, would you have any interest in it, my lord?” The more enterprising brother asked.

Rogan smiled and almost laughed. “No, young man, just curious,” he answered, spurring his horse. “Be careful. Where there is one, there usually is more,” he stated and watched as both boys nodded solemnly and moved to go back to work.

Before he could ride off, the taller boy called to him. “Are you following the precession my lord? If so, you are about three days behind them” and Rogan stopped, precession he wondered. “Why, yes can you tell me which way they went?” he asked now curious.

The boy pointed towards the direction Rogan was heading “that way, about twenty soldiers and a carriage, I think a high lords carriage from the craftsmanship” he said shaking his head “I mean the carvings were impressive” he mentioned and Rogan just nodded, looking towards the west now.

“Do you get many of them out this way?” Rogan asked with a forced nonchalance he didn’t feel, and the boy cocked his head in thought, his hands going to his belt loop which was absent a belt and hooked a finger in it absently.

“Not often, but I have seen that carriage before, about once every three months or so,” he called back, Rogan could see the worried look his brother shot at him.

It was not often commoners were approached by a lord and rarer still for one to have a conversation with so much familiarity with one.

Before his brother could step in, he simply nodded at the young man, reaching into his pocket and produced a silverling, flipping it to him, the young man caught it deftly and nodded his appreciation as Rogan rode off, following the direction of the caravan.

A high lord? He wondered, he would have known of a caravan moving through these parts, they would have requested a guard contingent from the palace and Rogan knew of every one of those requests, He also wasn’t using an airship as to avoid the royal navy, so he could only assume a covert meeting he thought, spurring his horse a little faster.

He now watched the woods with a bit more interest, it would not be wise to be caught off guard if another one of those cats were about, he chided himself.

One day he thought smiling the Empress would complete her mission. We will be able to go beyond just survival, we would have the weapons to drive back the big predators like that cat and be able to live like the ancients did with technology aiding in daily life allowing us to finally focus on more scholarly pursuits to help further humanity and not just scrape in the dirt for another potato or carrot.

He rode until the sun began to descend, his eyes every so often scanning the wood line warily, finally he chose a small clearing to camp for the night.

His sleep was uneventful, and Rogan was back on the road early the next morning, the day was already warmer than the previous and he was able to lay the large fur across the saddling giving his ride a bit more comfort, besides it freed up the sword and pistols that adorned his belt, if there was a caravan, and as he suspected black market dealers if the would-be hunters were to be believed, he did not want to run into them without access to a way to defend himself.

Rogan could feel his excitement growing the closer to the destination and to answers he sought, that would shed light on who and what was happening at the aptly named, Black Tower.

Finally, Cresting a ridge, the silhouette of a large stone tower stood in the shadow of the mid-day sun, even from a distance he could see smoke and activity rising from the courtyard, smiling in triumph, he had found what he had been searching for.

The wind carried the smell of burning wood and cooking meat across his path caressing the ornate red silk shirt he wore.

As he descended the small rise Rogan began to feel apprehension grow, he was alone and possibly encroaching somewhere that those who ran it would rather, as an official of the crown, he not know about, his hands absently checked the two ivory-handled resin pistols and black handled bastard sword on his belt, ensuring they were free and readily available, the tower began to loom as he approached, rising high into the sky, the profile of a squat two-story structure that supported it now visible just over the large stone wall that surrounded the complex.

Maybe I should have brought soldiers with me, he thought, reminding himself that even though the crown had paid the bills these soldiers might not appreciate that he was the one that wrote the checks. Especially if the owner of this structure wanted him silenced.

Pulling one of the ornate pistols, he gently laid it across the saddle, hiding it with the jacket as he draped a portion of it over his leg.

It wouldn’t offer protection from more than six guards, he knew once he spent the ammunition he would have no time to reload before he was shot or pulled off his horse, but the action made him feel better, before he could come his senses, Rogan urged the white horse faster towards the large stone wall.

Rogan could just make out people as they peered over the wall, pointing as others dashed around at the base, he had been noticed and none of the people looked happy about it he thought the smile faltering on his face as with grim determination he rode straight for the gate.

Rogan was pulled up short as he approached the two massive doors that stood as the entrance to the complex, he could now see that the large stone walls had been newly repaired and reinforced protected the dilapidated keep beyond.

Allowing his eyes to play over the structure revealed by the open gates he followed it up seeing the contours of the old tower, this close he could make out the breaks and cracks in the old stone that had stood here for over a century weathering the elements.

The two guards cautiously approached Rogan’s horse, “What is your business here?” the taller of the two stated, Rogan caught a distinctly eastern accent in his tone, odd he thought that would make this man either from Dever or further east he mused, his apprehension growing.

What was he doing guarding a gate in Vicor?

Were these even the Empress’s soldier he thought getting nervous as he spied the ten soldiers quickly assembling in the courtyard, plus these two severely outnumbered him and as of now, no one else knew where he was.

Mustering his courage, he stood fast as the guard approached, suspiciously eyeing him as he moved, his eyes never leaving Rogan’s, he would not cow the Lord Resolved, maintaining eye contact, these men were on his land, his territory and in his keep, they would give him answers he resolved sitting straighter on his horse and pushing down his doubt and fear with a sheer force of will.

Rogan noticed one of the guard’s hands fall to the butt of a pistol on his belt as did his friends. His own hand closed tightly around the one still sitting on his lap underneath the coat, quietly cocking it and keeping the wince off his face as he listened to the mechanical sound, he adjusted it carefully ensuring not to move the coat as the guard came around, Rogan doing his best to slowly move the barrel in the soldiers direction.

It wouldn’t be an accurate shot, but if this man became a threat Rogan was sure he could at least fell this guard before the other one ended his life, doubt as to his approach now settling into his mind, but knowing it was too late to turn back or run, these men would simply shoot him in the back, he would have to play this out.

The guard stopped short of Rogan’s saddle, settling his hands on the reigns as he looked up regarding the young Lord. “This is a private residence; you are going to have to turn around my lord” he stated.

Rogan could hear the edge in the man’s voice as well as see the tension in the others body language as he sat there, silently regarding both men for a moment.

If he hadn’t known they were hiding something, then he sure as hell would have suspected it by now. “I am Lord Juric Rogan, I am the Empress’s Chancellor and demand entry to this property, would you refuse the Empress’s emissary soldier” Rogan stated with as much authority as he could muster.

Leaning over he displayed the large gold ring on his middle finger upon which stood the lioness seal of the Empress on top of a hand. The symbol denoting his position and was the badge of his authority in the kingdom.

Rogan knew this would be the moment of truth, if they deemed him a threat or had orders to ensure secrecy, they could kill him and dump the body, he needed to dissuade that line of thinking he thought, looking down at the soldier he rose his voice so that all the soldiers would hear his next words.

“I also need to ensure you have sleeping accommodations and supplies to feed fifty soldiers, they should be here within the hour” he said eyeing the guard, willing the man to buy the lie.

The guard looked at the ring closely, after a moment he looked up to the Ramparts where another man stood, this one in a robe, his cowl up so Rogan could not see his face, following the guards gaze he eyed this man who looked like a monk, was this man in charge Rogan wondered trying to see his face under the dark hood.

After a moment the man’s hood moved slightly indicating agreement. Stepping away from the horse, the guard motioned Rogan to enter. “Welcome to the Tower my lord, anything you need just let us know and we will accommodate you” he said to the now surprised Lord.

Looking around he could see the other guards visibly relax, Rogan couldn’t help but think it was kind of trick and in fact he was only moments away from disappearing, he did his best to control the shaking hands and fast heartbeat caused by the dumping of adrenaline into his system.

Rogan brought the horse through the gates, noticing that the courtyard had been well taken care of, odd for such a dilapidated structure he mused.

Outside the large structure everything looked as if it were abandoned, but once inside he could see the signs of repairs and maintenance. Someone was ensuring this place was not only used, but also well-kept he thought guiding the horse into the stables, he noticed the new wood and beams that had been installed to repair the building.

Fresh hay and supplies stood in one corner though with only two other horses in the building he imagined there were patrols surveying the area but that still didn’t explain the discrepancy of the horse to soldier ratio, unless there was a permanent detachment or another stable, he wasn’t seeing.

This place was well hidden, well supplied and fortified, just the kind of place someone who was running a secret operation would want.

Dismounting his horse, Rogan started as a soldier simply appeared, the young Lord had not heard him approach. “What can we do for you my lord” the young soldier asked with a genuine smile spreading across his face, it took Rogan a moment to get his bearing.

Looking beyond the young soldier but not seeing the man with the robe and cowl, as if he had simply disappeared, from the look of it he was in charge and procedure dictated he should have been the one to greet someone as important as the Empress’s chancellor.

But Rogan did not push it, he wasn’t here for an ego stroke, but to find out what this place was and why it was here. “I need to find someone to give me a tour, some questions have been raised by the Empress as to the work done here and I will get to the bottom of this for her majesty” he stated again mustering as much authority for the white lie as he could as if his visit was planned and expected, if they bought it the likely hood they would simply execute him and hide the body would seem futile to them, he hoped.

The soldier didn’t even flinch, simply nodded and motioned Rogan to follow. As they left the stables The Chancellor began surveying the inside of the walls and courtyard noticing the repairs and reinforcement of the place as they moved closer to the entrance.

This place might be well maintained and repaired but everything he spied looked as if it had been done some time ago, this place had obviously been in operation for a long time he thought as they entered a thick wooden door on the main structure.

To his surprise, it was twice the thickness of any normal door and it had been recently replaced or repaired in the last few years.

The iron hinges glided effortlessly without a sound. Well-oiled he thought stepping into the building. Inside it was well kept though not built for comfort as only shelves of supplies a few tables and simple wooden chairs surrounded the large stone hearth, the rest of the space devoid of items save a few storage crates.

The soldier guided him further into the structure, motioning him to follow as he entered a narrow hall. Rogan stayed close, though out of arms reach of the soldier should he try and grab him.

He knew it was stupid, if these soldiers had wanted him gone or dead, they could have simply overwhelmed him, but it made him feel better as if he maintained some control of the situation.

They came to a door, one of several along the hall the soldier opened it without knocking, standing to the side he motioned Rogan forward.

“These will be your rooms while you are here my Lord, give us about thirty minutes and someone will come to ensure you get a detailed tour of the facility” he stated in an official tone and waited as Rogan stood there eyeing the room suspiciously.

A moment later Rogan realized that he had been standing there eyeing both the soldier and the room far longer than he should have, and it was beginning to get uncomfortable, the soldier doing his best to not look as irritated as he probably felt.

Finally, resolving himself to trust these soldiers as least in the fact that they did not have to display a false pretense to deal with someone like him.

He entered the room as the soldier closed the door behind him gently and then Rogan could hear his footsteps fade as he walked back towards the front of the building. Checking the door, he half expected it to be locked, but as he depressed the handle, he felt it open slightly and sighed with relief, turning he inspected the room.

It was a large room with a four poster bed and a desk, he studied the craftsmanship, it looked oddly familiar, in fact it looked as if the same artisan had carved this set as had done the ones in his own room in the capital, this just got curiouser and curiouser he thought.

He wouldn’t call it opulent, but it would suffice he decided. Rogan spent the next forty minutes searching the drawers of the desk and under the bed for items, weapons or information, finding nothing he eventually gave up, opting to simply sit on the large bed looking at the four drab grey stone walls as he waited impatiently for someone to come retrieve him, he considered leaving, searching the complex, but that would not be in standing with his authority or reason for being here, he would wait, allow them to show him the facility as would any dignitary assigned this detail.

He was just about to go find someone when a soft knock came at the door and with an annoyed sigh, he Stormed over to it throwing it open his anger quickly dying as Rogan regarded the silent robed figure from the balcony standing before him.

The man was slightly taller than Rogan’s own six feet, though he seemed to loom despite this, his cowl casting a dark shadow over the area where his face was, the effect made it look as if the entire robe was filled simply with darkness, the man stood silent, adding to effect, neither man talking as time stretched to the point of awkward, Rogan took an involuntary step back, something about this man felt wrong, the feeling spilling off of the robed figure in waves.

He did not make a threatening move just stood there resplendent in his silence, Rogan took ye another involuntary step back cursing himself for his fear and weakness, but not moving closer either, the hairs on the back of his neck stood on end in warning.

“Lord Juric Rogan, I am Vincent, I am the keeper and Administrator of the tower and bid you welcome, we have been expecting you for some time” Vincent said, his voice like nails on a chalkboard grated against the inside of Rogan’s skull, it was all he could do to not wince at the man.

His blood went cold as he played the statement over in his head, what did Vincent mean expecting him, how the hell had they known he was coming he wondered panic welling up in his gut, as he did his best to will his sight beyond the blackness under the cowl and see the man’s face, does he even have a face? Rogan wondered, suddenly looking down at the floor, it was a question he suddenly didn’t need answered.

Thinking through the man’s words he felt relief pass over him as his political mind processed every phrase, every word.

Vincent was doing what most administrators did, trying to convince his betters that he was in full control of the situation, fully knowledgeable of anything happening within or without of his property, this simple realization, the ability to attribute familiar human failings to this Specter of a man, gave him a marginal feeling of comfort allowing him to get control of himself as his own political animal took control of the conversation.

Rogan nodded proffering an amiable, albeit false smile. “Of course, I assume you are here to give me a tour of your facilities” he said dismissively, trying to sound casual as if it were business as usual, but he could still feel the fear nibbling at the corners of his mind.

The robed figure said nothing, simply motioned for him to follow, turning he glided down the hall, leaving Rogan to catch up as the figure walked quickly back towards the front of the facility, they approached the main room and Vincent’s gravelly voice rang off the walls as he spoke he effect giving his words an almost ethereal quality.

“I’m very glad you’re here Juric, I have so looked forward to meeting you” Vincent stated as they entered the main hall steering away from the large front entrance and instead towards a large iron door that Rogan had not noticed upon his arrival.

Looked forward to meeting me? He thought trying to get a look at Vincent’s face yet again, without success, but as he studied the cowl, a sliver a light danced over it cutting through the darkness and revealing a sliver of pale, human skin.

Rogan could make out scars along the man’s throat, though that wasn’t right he realized to his horror, they weren’t’ scars but symbols, someone had carved symbols into this man’s neck, who would allow that to be done to themselves he wondered, the answer hung just out of reach in the recess of his mind, then suddenly, crystalizing as the fear continued to swell within his belly.

Zealot his mind echoed Rogan frozen by indecision continued to follow this man, this zealot. “Really, I don’t think we have met, but I see my reputation precedes me” Rogan stated nervously as he projected his voice a little too loudly, trying to fill the cavernous silence and eliciting a sardonic chuckle from Vincent.

“No Lord Rogan, we have not, but I have heard so much about you, it is good that you have come. It is time you know what is to come...” he said stepping up to the large iron door.

Slamming his fist against the thick wood three times, causing Rogan to jump, Vincent did not seem to notice or care, the hollow thud of his knocks muffled but still clear as they echoed on the far side of the entrance.

After a moment Rogan heard the familiar sound as metal scraped against wood the lock sliding and releasing the door. It smoothly swung open Vincent motioning for Rogan to follow, for a moment he almost didn’t, almost turned and ran simply leaving this place, but his curiosity, his desperate need for answers outweighed the fear and slowly Rogan put one foot in front of the other, repeating the action, following Vincent into the darkness on the far side of the door, his mind begging for him to get out.

Stepping through the entrance, Rogan stopped the lack of light making it hard to discern anything beyond a few inches from his face, after a moment his vision adjusted revealing a small, cramped stairwell, the ancient stone stood covered in a purple moss that looked slick to the touch, on the far end of the cramped anti-chamber stood an opening in the floor, Rogan carefully moved over to it, spotting the first sets of moss-covered steps descending down into the lower parts of the old keep.

Looking around he realized he was the only person standing within the small chamber, he lowered his head towards the stairway, straining his ears he heard the muffled steps as Vincent had already started down Who opened the door? he wondered, eyeing the large wooden slap.

Magic, his mind answered with alarm was Vincent a Mage, if so, is that why he hid he face Rogan wondered.

He had seen the carved runes in the man’s neck, but only for a second, he desperately tried to recall if he had seen Vincent’s cheek and possibly the Mage’s mark that he was now convinced would be there, with a resigned sigh, knowing with the guards, he would never make it out, not alive anyway he began to carefully descend the old stairs.

A blast of cold stale air rose from below, The smell of decay and body odor assaulted his senses causing the bile in his stomach to rise threatening to evacuate his body, managing to keep it down, but barely he breathed through his mouth to prevent a repeat of the vile odor.

What is this place? he wondered, carefully stepping down the ancient stone stairs, this man had thrown him off, put him off his game, and frankly, if he was being honest with himself, the whole experience scared the shit out of him.

What the hell is going on? Rogan wondered. With each step he moved into the facility, becoming less likely to successfully escape with his life. It was beginning to dawn on him he should have heeded his friend’s advice. Whatever was happening here, Rogan did not think he wanted to know about it. Continuing down the stairs, he did his best to contain his fear, each step down a struggle.

A scream erupted from below tearing at his soul as he almost lost control, he took two stumbling steps upwards before regaining it stopping himself from fleeing blindly back up the stairs, the scream hung in the air reverberating around him.

It was the sound of pain, hopelessness and anger he thought forcing himself down another step towards the soul curdling cry. He heard his guide from below as the echo of his chuckle resounded up the stairs. “They are restless, Lord Rogan, and they know you are coming. They can sense you,” Vincent merrily stated.

Rogan almost yelled at the man; his comments were disturbing his calm as fear coursed through his body. He forced his body further down the stairs, now the only thing lighting his way was crystal lamps hung every five feet. As he descended the natural light began to fade causing him to slow down even further to keep from sliding on the moss-covered steps.

Finally, reaching the bottom the stairs the room opened up into an identical small foyer as above with yet another of the thick wooden doors standing between him and the rest of the lower level, is this where I find answers? Rogan thought to himself as he recalled the scream and shivered, the better question he reflected do I want to know the answers?

The robed figure beat his fist on the door three times. Wails and screams rose like a demented chorus sending Rogan’s blood cold, the fear was so overwhelming his left foot involuntarily turned back towards the stairs as if it alone would flee, abandoning the rest of his body.

A moment later metal slid on metal and the massive door opened slowly, iron hinges loudly protested against its weight. As the door finally finished swinging interrupted by a stone wall, Rogan flinched as the heavy wood connected loudly with the stone revealing a disheveled guard who quickly bowed at the sight of Vincent “Keeper,” he simply said but the reverence in his tone did not go unnoticed by Rogan curious he thought, again the word Fanatic echoed in his mind.

What is a Keeper? he thought not recognizing the title. Vincent simply ignored the guard walking past him as if he wasn’t even there. Stopping just in the door, he waited for Rogan to move, it took the chancellor a few moments for the young lord to forcefully turn his left foot back towards the opening and step inside Vincent moved further into the dark hallway as Rogan joined him. The smell of body odor, feces and death assaulted his nose, once again he forced the bile back into his stomach, covering his nose.

Vincent didn’t seem to even notice the smell as he continued forward into yet another dark stone corridor, Rogan stopped short upon entering, looking up and down he long hallway he could make out thick iron doors lining both walls, spaced every eight feet apart.

Walking over to one, he laid his hand on it studying the ancient metal and took a mental step back realizing where he was, these are prison cells he thought.

Rogan could now hear the echoes, moans and growling coming from the cells, they were occupied, He suddenly didn’t want to know what was in those cells, his mind protesting, demanding he leave this place as the sounds were animalistic in nature, the hairs on the back of his neck jumped, coming to attention as fear crawled over his mind, whatever was in there didn’t sound human.

The keeper, without regard to the sounds, walked down the hall, stopping in front of one particular door and turned, smiling back at Rogan he regarded the young lord silently for a moment.

What was this man and what was he to this place Rogan wondered? Before he could follow that thought. Vincent took two steps towards one of the cell doors, throwing the lock, he swung the door open causing Rogan to jump back a little, but nothing came out at them, instead the opening stood empty, only the sounds of those things emanating from the blackness.

With a theatrical flourish of his hand Vincent invited Rogan to look inside.

Juric Rogan had never wanted to flee from somewhere so much in his entire life, turning he found the guard standing there smiling, blocking his only escape, He was trapped and his only option was forward he realized.

Swearing silently, he willed himself towards the opening, but not too close he wasn’t going to be trapped, if these two tried to throw him into the cell he would fight until they killed him he vowed, eyeing Vincent suspiciously, but neither he nor the guard make any movement to restrain him.

Keeping his hand on the edge of the stone wall as if it were a lifebuoy and he were a drowning man his fingers protested as he tightened his grip his fingertips white from the pressure.

Swinging around the edge of the door frame, he saw a dingy, dirty stone cell, ancient and rusted iron rings hung along three of the four walls, the kind you would string chains through to hold someone he thought, then a motion caught his eye, something moved in the back of the cell along the shadowed wall, Rogan tried to get a glimpse of the prisoner, stepping forward he peered towards the thing as it continued to hang in the shadows, slowly the prisoner leaned forward bringing its head into the light.

“Lord Aurtus, save me” Rogan breathed, taking an involuntary step back as he stared in open shock and horror, the creature stared back, open hostility in those soulless black eyes, he heard shuffling and Rogan realized It was not alone as others began to shuffle forward into the light.

The creatures loosely resembled humans in the fact that they were standing upright with two arms and two legs, but that is where the similarities ended.

Studying the tallest of the four creatures that had moved foward, its skin was a sickly pale as if it had never seen sunlight, he could see the creatures ribs along its naked torso, its elbows pronounced and even its skeletal framework was visible as if the skin had been pulled too tight over its body.

Slowly it turned towards the door and Rogan’s breath caught in his throat. Its black eyes regarded him with contempt, it took two steps forward, its eyes never leaving Rogan’s as it rose to its full six-foot height, anger radiated off of the creature in waves.

A low growl emanated from its throat and it took another step forward, bringing its entire body into the sliver of light.

To his horror, Rogan realized it was a female, though she only wore a loin cloth, her thin frame no longer had the body fat to support breasts and the skin hung flatly against her ribcage. Another of the creatures came to stand next to the female and Rogan turned his attention to it, realizing much to his horror that is was a child, it was her child he thought.

The child-creature stood close to its mother, hissing at the small group of people like a feral cat. Moving his eyes up to their skulls Rogan noticed the glint coming off their forehead realizing at once it was a piece of crystal, the wound around it told the story, someone had driven it into the creatures forehead, though he could not understand why, what were these things he wondered, his mind refusing to acknowledge that which he already suspected, they had been people once, like him, people with lives until something here had transformed them into these things.

“What happened to them?” Rogan whispered not able to keep the horror and revulsion out of his voice. The keeper didn’t bother turning toward Rogan, but he could clearly hear Vincent’s raspy low voice in the dungeon’s hallway as it echoed off the stone walls unencumbered by decorations or furniture.

“Sometimes in the pursuit of greatness, mistakes happen and then even those mistakes come to have a use” he simply said.

Rogan didn’t respond, instead continuing to study the creatures.

Something was wrong with their skin, as he looked, he could make out black blotches covering the entire bodies of both the creatures.

Squinting he tried to get a better look without getting too close. Something about the blotches told him they were not something natural, there was a pattern to them.

Then they came into focus as the woman took four steps towards the door putting herself in between Rogan and her child, the maternal action driving home the point that this thing had once been a happy human with a family, Rogan almost gagged when he realized that those blotches were symbols, black symbols someone had carved into their skin, realization dawning, he had seen those same symbols on the Robed Keeper.

“How could someone do this?” he asked emotion choking up his voice. The female tilted her head to the ceiling and let out a scream full of hate and hopelessness and as she did, every other cell erupted with similar screams.

There had to be over a hundred creatures here. Rogan thought of someone doing this to people, turning them into these…things. “What sort of evil magic is this Keeper, why was this done to the Empress’s subjects” Rogan asked, his tone was firm and promised pain should he not like the answer as anger replaced the fear and revulsion.

Turning, Rogan took a step towards the Keeper, he was going to make this man answer for this, this travesty that had been perpetrated against these people when another voice from behind him stopped him short, but it was impossible he thought, that voice couldn’t be here.

“I am the one who authorized it, Lord Rogan. I am the one who takes responsibility for it, and I am the one who found another use for these research failures.

I told you I would do anything to save mankind. And I meant it,” said the voice and Rogan turned to find the Empress standing there in the middle of the hall, he had been so focused on the creatures he had not heard her arrive, standing there unbelieving for a moment, trying to understand how she was here, how she was part of this.

From reflex he went to his knee, bowing before the empress. “My Empress,” he said, not knowing what else to say. How could he question her on the actions she had taken, but then another voice within him said How can you not? He was rendered silent from indecision, so Rogan simply knelt, his mind warring with itself, trying to understand what was happening, he tried to think of what to do and what to say.

He heard the click of her small boots as she came towards him, he felt the soft touch of her fingers on his chin as she lifted him off the ground, standing a head taller than the woman it was still easy to tell who in that room had the power, it was as if her personality filled every vacant space in the small dungeon.

“I know you have questions; I know you feel anger and I understand. I needed to bring you here Juric, I needed you to see before I could really explain it to you. As I have said, I will do whatever I need to, to save mankind, to ensure we as a race do not become extinct. These people, my subjects are a sacrifice towards that, one I initially regretted, but they have a use and a critical role to play, just as we all in this room do. Come let us adjourn upstairs and I will answer all of your questions” she finished smiling up at the young Lord.

The Keeper closed the cell mercifully hiding the faces of the monstrous creatures. As Rogan allowed himself to be led by his Empress. He was tired, he couldn’t think how she was here, did she orchestrate his finding of this place and if so, why, his mind unable to comprehend the last few minutes as it scrambled to try and fill in answers, tried to cope with everything around him, he felt he would go mad as he walked, following the woman who was his Empress, his blind faith and trust the only thing keeping him from rebelling and fighting to fling open cells and free these poor pathetic beings.

These questions and more ran through his mind as he ascended the stairs, making his way to the building above.

She took his hand and he felt the cool, gentle, confident grip of the woman he worshipped and loved, the woman who had taken him in, trained him, gave him a position that showed trust and respect, how could he question her now, how could he doubt her.

Rogan thought as she led him upstairs and past his room, entering another set of circular stairs leading up. Randomly he thought, I am going to the tower.

They ascended walking in a tight circle as they followed the tower to the top. Once there the Empress opened the door, the room was warm and relaxing, covered in dark wood and furs, the furniture was basic but comfortable it looked like a place someone would go to get away.

There was none of the ostentation of the throne room or her sleeping chambers back in the capital, but it still had a sense of the lavish. Victoria led him over to a chair, gently pushing on him to sit, he obliged.

Rogan was still in shock, his minding racing trying to put together some coherent thought from everything that had happened. None of the others followed, they remained on the first floor leaving the Empress and Rogan alone in the tower.

Victoria pulled the red piece of silk from her hair, allowing the full five feet of the blond mane to descend over her back, it gave her a very disarmingly beautiful look, one that was relaxed and much less official than usual causing Rogan to unconsciously relax as well.

She took the chair next to him, leaning in close and flashing a gentle and reassuring smile.

He regarded his Empress, her eyes held worry though he didn’t know if it was for him, or for her plans.

“Why?” he whispered, the word both a question and an accusation. It was as close to insubordination as he had ever come, and in that one word was everything, everything he wanted to know. Everything he needed to know. Why him? Why them? Why now? Every why his mind couldn’t resolve was in that one question.

Sighing, the Empress leaned back looking towards the window and collecting her thoughts. Rogan just regarded her. She was like a mother, an older sister or the object of everything he wanted in a woman.

She was everything, and he would do anything to protect her, to serve her, and to ensure her will was done. That had always been his way, his mandate, his mission, but as he tried to resolve what he had seen and place it in the grand architecture that was his world. Those people he thought as doubt in his Empresses mission sprouted within his mind, the feeling was foreign to him, but there it was none the less, how could anyone justify what had been done to them he thought.

He needed her to explain, to tell him it was going to be okay, to explain that it was for the greater good before his moral foundation crumbled into dust. Finally, the Empress turned towards him smiling that reassuring smile that always made everything better, he needed everything to be better his mind screamed.

“Juric, when I took you in, I knew about your power, I know it’s not much, but it is a gift, one your family did not understand, nor would they have encouraged it. But that made you special, special to me and to helping me save our race” she began and Rogan sat bolt upright he had spent his entire life hiding his meek ability, ensuring that no one ever saw what he could do, yet now, his Empress knew, who else did, he wondered panic beginning to grow in his gut as he thought about the brand that would adorn his cheek marking him as a mage, damning him to his peers.

“How did you know” he gasped ashamed that she would know about his little secret but relieved that there was no judgment in her words or face. No, she had called it important he thought sitting up straighter.

“That doesn’t matter, but I understand what it’s like” she continued and then the Empress did something that awed Rogan as he watched she extended her arm and a small box on the table levitated to her. She grasped the box as it floated close to her palm her eyes locking with his. “I understand what it’s like,” she reiterated but Rogan was beyond hearing, he was beyond anything.

The Empress had a gift like his, well stronger than his but she would understand. “We are gifted Juric, we are the future of our race, its people like us that will save everyone else, we are made great, the born leaders of mankind.

Most don’t like us, they fear us, they want to control us or kill us, there are groups out there that keep themselves secret, but they all want to ensure we are no longer able to dictate our own existence Juric, so we keep ourselves secret, we keep hidden so we do not have to bear the mark of the mage, the mark of shame,” she continued, standing and walking to the window.

The sun caught her golden hair and Rogan thought at that moment she was the most beautiful creature in existence as he sat there enjoying the view. But his brain was like a torrential storm as reason and morality warred with idealism and fanaticism as he tried to process and keep up with what the Empress was saying.

She was right they were special, well she was Rogan could barely lift a pen with his gift, but didn’t that put them above the mundane inhabitants of this land, those who didn’t share their abilities, weren’t they given this for some reason, some destiny he thought.

She turned back to him, coming to stand only feet from the chair. “Juric, you know I have collected ancient books, books from those of the first men, books from groups who are so secret you have never even heard their names, groups so threatening no one even dares whisper about them, groups that even the learned men of this time cringe and refuse to speak of, these groups still hold sway, their theories shaping the foundation of our society.

I have used my collection, studying the scholars who understood our magic on such an intimate level they could manipulate the very blueprint of our bodies with their will.

I have coopted their work to make those of us better, stronger, preparing us and making us ready to guide our people through the coming threat,” she began and then her face fell, he could see the hurt and guilt as she sat back in chair.

“But there have been setbacks and mistakes, you have now seen the worst of them, in my vanity to make our people better I have turned some of my subjects into monsters” she began and then locking eyes with Rogan he saw the guilt change to a fire of determination and resolve.

“But they have their uses, they will be our enforcers Rogan, they will help us ensure we are in charge and are able to fight off those who would try to stop us” she finished.

Rogan could believe it, he could see the monster below as a necessary sacrifice, swallowing the guilt and shock he focused on the bigger view, her words reigniting the fire of determination as it purified his own resolve, burning away the doubt and guilt, they would change the kingdom, using it as a launching point to taking control of the other dominances, bringing them under one rule, her rule, they would save them from the coming storm and in doing so preserving humanity.

Of course, he thought the people who saved mankind should be those with the gift, those the gods entrusted the power to he thought nodding at the Empress.

She smiled at him happy he understood. Of course, he understood he thought, how could he have doubted her. Then her face became solemn. “Thing are about to change Juric and I need you, I need you to help me take control of the corrupt government my husband had fostered, the one I have tried to fight against for the last decade, we are ready to come out of hiding to run this kingdom without those who would question or scheme or work against us” she finished.

Rogan understood, she was right he had seen it, hell he had taken care of a lot of them, ensured they never bothered her or tried to conspire against her again.

“What can I do to serve you better, my Empress?” Rogan breathed, and a smile spread across her face. “Your journey is just beginning Juric, I will make you one of my chosen, you will be one of my inner circle, my knights,” she stated, her face becoming solemn.

“But the journey will be painful my little lord, with transformation comes pain, but you have been training for this day all your life, I have ensured you were schooled in everything you needed to know so that this day, you would be ready, will you serve me Juric, will you trust me, will you endure the pain of change so that you can become my knight,” she said and then saw a flash of doubt as Rogan thought about the creatures in the dungeon, would that be him he wondered and as if she were reading his mind.

The Empress shook her head. “No, my young Lord, those are soldiers, you will not be them, that is not your destiny, you will be transformed, but you will still be you” she finished and Rogan couldn’t nod fast enough, whatever pain, whatever trials he had to complete he would to ensure her will was served.

The Empress looked beyond him, and Rogan heard the door open, turning he found two more of the black-robed figures, their cowls up to hide their faces as they stood sentry on either side of the door.

“They are to be your brothers Juric, you will become like them” she stated nodding to the robed figures. In unison, the two extended their arms, Rogan watched as the two chairs in the center of the room began to levitate, the two robed figures standing stalwart as the steady hands lifted towards the ceiling in unison carrying the chairs with them, Rogan felt his heart fall at the sight of this.

“But, my Empress, I don’t have that kind of power, mine is weak,” he said, defeated and shamed as the young Lord hung his head.

The Empress smiled at him. “Juric, this journey you will take will be painful you will have doubt, but if you complete it, then you will be one of the most powerful gifted alive, your power will nearly approach the first of us” then her face changed.

A glint appearing in her eye as she smiled “as for the first, there is one among us, a fallen Juric, one who I have been in contact with, I hope to bring him into the fold” she finished Rogan looked to her, not comprehending her meaning, he was about to question her when she stood, motioning for Rogan to do the same, motioning him to follow the Empress walked over to the two figures, they gently put their hands on his arms, guiding him out of the room and down the stairs, looking back he could see the Empress standing there in the doorway, smiling approvingly at him as he descended the spiral staircase.

The trio walked out of the building, the two robed figures bookending Rogan, gently guiding him across the courtyard, both men showing a surprising amount of reverence in dealing with him, he thought, eyeing the two as they moved into a small stone building.

Entering the stone structure, Rogan surveyed the open area, It was a simple structure, the entire building was a single room, stone walls and floors gave it a muted earthy feel, looking up he could see the large wooden rafters which showed signs of recent repair, The room stood mostly empty, save for a podium holding a large leatherbound book and an old medical bed, similar to the ones used in hospitals he thought, looking closely he could make out straps where the head, arms and legs would go, approaching it carefully, Rogan ran his hand over the old wood feeling the gouges and scratches carved into the wood, whoever had used this had thrashed and a lot from the feel of it he thought, fear began to sprout deep in his stomach as he looked over the old bed thinking of what they must have gone through, what he would go through.

What did I agree to, what are they going to do to me? he wondered. He could feel his heard trying to leap from his chest and took a long calming breath, leaning over he studied the straps closely, seeing signs of wear and the dark stains that looked suspiciously like dried blood across the hand-tooled leather, someone had been in them and had struggled hard.

He had done enough ‘questioning’ for the Empress to recognize the twists and wear patterns from someone twisting wrists and pulling against the straps.

Am I to become like those creatures? he wondered. Fear continuing to plague him despite the Empress’s reassurances, his trust and determination to please the Empress mitigated that fear, but only just.

“This will hurt,” rasped the first robed figure, Rogan caught the motion of a nod as the second man’s cowl moved in affirmation.

“This will make you better,” said the second,

Climbing up on the table Rogan did his best to relax as the two robed figures went about binding him, every time a limb was secured Rogan felt panic once again try and rear its ugly head, once he was on the table, the two went about checking the straps to ensure they were securely fastened, he felt the final strap across his forehead as they tightened it, the pressure causing a minor headache.

Moving around he tested the straps, again came the panic at his inability to move.

“What is going to happen?” Rogan asked nervously trying his best to keep his tone casual but wincing when his voice broke in fear. “Relax Juric, we all went through this, we all survived” came a familiar voice from the shadows, he tried to move his head to get a look at the person talking, but couldn’t, so instead rotated his eyes searching out the source, he knew that voice he thought.

Another robed figure emerged from the shadows, Rogan did not know if he had been there the entire time or not, but his steps were silent as he appeared to glide out into the light, almost like a ghost.

The robed Specter threw back his hood to reveal a smiling face that Rogan recognized. Of course, it would be him, he thought.

“I not surprised that you are here, pulling the strings spymaster” he stated regarding the old unassuming man.

He stared at Rogan for a few minutes, his eyes held kindness, seeing this Rogan slightly relaxed, he tried to look around the room unsuccessfully.

Jurin caught his glance and smiled reassuringly at the young lord, “It’s okay, this is not the first time they have done this my friend”,

Turning he pointed to the ancient and yellowing book that sat upon the podium.

“That book,” came from an order of people like us who have spent the last few generations perfecting the symbols like these” He stated pulling up his sleeve and showing the carved runic symbols on his arm.

The Spymaster moved over to a bowl of water that sat upon the floor, just inside Rogan’s peripheral vision, and with a quick motion of his hand plucked a rag from it, the bronze-colored bowl tottering at the removal of the weight and spilling some of the water on the floor, Jurin didn’t seem to notice, or care.

He began to rub his face, at first gently and then with more effort. As Rogan watched, makeup that had been carefully applied began to wash off, revealing more of the obsidian symbols carved all over his face, he shivered at the view, noticing the deeps wounds as if they had been gouged into the man’s ancient leather skin, the area around the symbols looking hard, like old scarring, the black letters made more visible by the alabaster scar tissue that surrounded it, like his arms the symbols covered his head and neck.

Rogan had seen those symbols, or ones like them. His mind going back to the faces of the creatures below, another shiver ran through his body as he recognized a few of the obsidian runes having been on both the old Spymaster and the mother-creature in the dungeon and he was reminded both had started right here, on this table, which one will I become? he wondered.

Jurin turned to regard the young man, allowing Rogan to study the strange runic symbols, he quickly noticed a pattern to their placement, giving Jurin lines of Runic script dividing his face into six parts lengthwise.

“This group discovered that our abilities can be enhanced when they are shaped through a combination of runes the same language the mages use to create the spells applied to objects, the power molded and reformed, redoubled and focused as it flows to our will, however, we went one step beyond.” He began, Before Rogan could ask the question, Jurin continued not waiting for the query.

“By creating a crystal resin mixed with various other chemicals, we developed a flexible material that, once dry, fuses with your skin, becoming part of it, it won’t chip, it won’t peel off, enhancing your power by an order of magnitude my friend, but the process, is painful.” he finished.

“How does it even do that; how can you create a crystal liquid that does these things?” Rogan asked, he was curious but mostly it was to keep his mind off of what was about to be done to him.

Jurin shrugged. “I am not a scientist my lord, but what I do know is, these crystals are not of this world, they are a product of what happened to the ancients, the last testament to a world we can never understand, these crystals have special properties, when you are able to merge or bring close the right combination of these crystals, they react. Similar to the crystal lanterns we use every day.” But even our knowledge of the crystals and what they can do is rudimentary at best.

Rogan nodded, there was a vast distance between a simple lantern and something as complex as this he thought.

The two other robed figures pulled down their hoods revealing faces covered in the same obsidian symbols, Rogan did not recognize these two but it was as if someone had a template, these men, Jurin included looked as if they were created using the same process, the bald head, the lined runic script, hell even down to their pallor and shared grim expression.

They looked like holy men, some type of twisted order that forced their members to be branded and marked proving their devotion through pain.

Was this some kind of secular order? he thought, and then dismissed it, the Empress was a lot of things, but zealot was not one of them.

How many times had the two of them sat around the Empress’s chambers poking fun at the messenger’s in the capital or some of the stories he would tell about his time interviewing with the church?

No this wasn’t a religion at least not in the traditional sense he thought, one of the men came over and began to gently undress Rogan.

Becoming alarmed he looked to Jurin who shot him another reassuring smile, Rogan relaxed allowing this man to continue to remove his clothes, until he lay upon the table naked.

He tried not to give in to the insecurities of being exposed in a room full of men. The old spymaster approached, picking up another bowl and began to cut at Rogan’s long hair, he felt the sharp blade scraping the skull as the man gently shaved his head.

Once he was done, Rogan lay there, his head cold, his scalp not having seen the light of day since infancy, turning his head he could see the two figures standing at a table behind the podium, one that Rogan had not noticed before, as he watched the two men moved over to the podium, taking various small crystal spires, with expert precision and patience they gently chipped away at them with a delicate-looking hammer.

Carefully and deliberately they took the small pile of multicolored chips, placing them into a mortar and pestle, Rogan continued to watch with a detached, almost clinical fascination.

One of the men began to mix what looked like dark ink into the mortar, slowly he brought the pestle down, the grinding of the crystal causing Rogan to wince at the unpleasant sound.

Once the mixture was done, one of the figures carried it slowly over to where Rogan was strapped to the table.

Laying the bowl down next to him, he took a small brush and began to meticulously paint symbols on Rogan’s naked body, the liquid was cold, almost uncomfortable at first and then becoming strangely pleasant, as the man finished a symbol, he would lightly blow on it to dry it so it wouldn’t run, the action causing gooseflesh to rise on his body, the feeling almost erotic.

Closing his eyes, he controlled his breathing as he concentrated on the feeling and pushing away the errant worries and fear.

“Don’t move, it has to be precise” Jurin called coming to stand next to the large wooden table that Rogan lay strapped on, the spymaster laid a hand gently, almost in paternal fashion on Rogan’s shoulder. “We need to ensure we have them correct before we inlay them into your flesh.” he stated as he gave his shoulder a reassuring squeeze.

The process took over three hours but when the man was done Rogan was covered from head to toe in drawn symbols organized in lines over his entire person.

Jurin closed his eyes, reaching down and gently touching Rogan’s head.

He felt the familiar vibration as magic coursed through him, the old man concentrated, pushing more power through Rogan, the vibration increasing as he felt it deep within his body, seeming to vibrate every organ and extremity.

Jurin opened his eyes looking down at the young Lord and smiled, Rogan peered down following the old man’s gaze, and gasped, the symbols pulsated, glowing bright green and then going dark.

Most of them glowed brightly but some were only half glowing or completely dark, these the first man began to draw over, fixing or adjusting, as he completed his work, the symbol would fully light and he would move to the next one, every symbol checked and recheck with expert precision.

“We have gotten very good at this my lord” Jurin breathed continuing to push power through the young lord’s body. “What do they all mean?” Rogan asked still trying to get a look at them. Jurin opened his eyes and thought for a moment and at first, he didn’t think the spymaster would answer but finally he spoke.

“Some of these are focus strings, allowing you to focus your will enhancing the distance and power of your gift, it takes your initial energy, in your case the very limited amount of power you are able to summon and doubles it, over and over, allowing it to grow in strength before entering this, the focus line” he stated, pointing to another set of runic script” this is how we make you stronger.

Finally, there is an armor spell woven through the others, this ensures protection against energy or kinetic power.

Do not worry Rogan, it will come naturally to you, do not be afraid.” He finished, Rogan nodded, not really understanding what the old spymaster was talking about, this was far beyond his knowledge of magic he realized, the small spark of fear returning despite the man’s reassurance.

Looking down he eyed the symbols, the dark color making it look like dried blood, the thought not calming him at all.

The two men worked tirelessly, mixing in small bowls as they checked and confirmed with the old text, once in a while, making small changes to the solution they finally seemed ready.

They nodded at Jurin who produced a small box from the folds of his robes.

Walking over to Rogan he laid the small box down gently next to him.

He began to work in the box finally pulling out a small brown ball the size of a pea.

“Take this and put it under your tongue, let it dissolve, it will help with the pain” he said his smile was gentle and with a nod Rogan did as he asked. The taste was incredibly bitter, but he let it sit there, the digestive acids beginning to soften and break down the thing under his tongue.

“How much will it hurt?” Rogan asked, his voice slightly distorted as he tried not to move his tongue. Jurin winced and that was all the answer Rogan needed.

The two others came over, gently laying down the bowl as they placed odd knives along the edge of the table. Rogan would have gotten nervous, even scared.

But the oddest thing began to happen, He felt a calming warmth spreading down his body, a feeling of happiness began to descend upon his mind as he felt sleepy, fighting to stay awake he watched with a detached interest as the men began to choose between the sharp curved silver blades on the table.

With complete concentration they each placed cold blades against Rogan’s torso in tandem, he felt the pinch as the knives bit into his body, warm wetness trickled down his body as blood began to flow from the cuts.

The men gently wiping the wounds clean as they continued to carve out the drawn symbols on him, constantly cutting and dabbing the blood away with efficient patience.

This process seeming to go on forever, Rogan staring at the ceiling.

The pressure of the blades and the dabbing of cloth his only companion, finally they completed the task of carving the symbols, carefully tracing the ink they had laboriously applied to his body, both men picked up small pitchers, dabbing the blood one final time they began to fill the wounds with a black shiny liquid.

Rogan felt the cold, thick liquid slightly burning as it settled into the cut, drying into the wound. Jurin came over and placed another of the balls into Rogan’s mouth and as it began to break down, darkness descended upon him as he fell into a deep drug induced sleep.

Awaking some hours later, his skin pulsing with pain as he lay there, Rogan ran his tongue against his upper palate, the feeling akin to sandpaper he thought.

“Here drink this, this will help with the pain” came a raspy voice, Rogan looked up to see Vincent, his hood drawn back to reveal his gaunt face, taking the vial from him he drank, wincing at the bitter taste of the clear liquid.

A few moments later the ache subsided, but he remained clear headed unlike the brown balls that Jurin had given to him. “Is it done?” Rogan asked, his voice cracking from thirst.

Vincent walked over to the table and poured a cup of water, returning he poured cold water slowly down Rogan’s throat. The liquid began to permeate the soft tissue, rehydrating it, laying back he closed his eyes, Rogan felt tired, but he couldn’t tell if that was from the process or an after effect of the drugs.

Vincent broke into his thoughts “It is done” he simply said, Rogan lifted his arm, turning it over and looking at the symbols now inlaid into the skin realizing for the first time, he was no longer tied down.

Lifting his other arm, he touched the skin on his cheek gently, feeling the symbols, they were cold and hard, looking closer at the arm he could see his skin had healed by knitting into the substance, fusing it with his skin, each symbol was surrounded by white scar tissue like he had seen on Jurin.

He twisted his arm experimentally and watched as the symbols also flexed and stretched, coming back into their original shape, the feeling was strange, he could tell where his skin ended and the symbol began, but it didn’t hurt, only odd he reflected twisting his arm again and watching the symbols react with fascination.

It looked like someone had laid obsidian stone into his arm, but it was pliable and flexible enough to move with his skin, not restricting it.

“This is amazing,” he whispered with wonder as he continued to flex his arm and feel the substance flex with it.

Vincent smiled, the action was genuine, it actually made his face look more personable. “You have not seen anything yet my young Lord” he said moving back to the table and putting away the tools they had used for the procedure.

Rogan lay there for another thirty minutes allowing the drugs to leave his system when finally, the door opened and the Empress walked into the room, smiling at Rogan, he couldn’t help but smile back.

“How is our patient?” she asked Vincent who bowed his head slightly in respect “He is well my Empress, ready for you to show him” he finished, Rogan looked between the two, confused “show me what?” he asked and she motioned for him to join her.

Rogan slowly got up off the table, Reaching up he ran his hand through his hair except, it was no longer there, his hand touching his scalp, the tips of his fingers running over the raised shapes of the runic symbols embedded in his skin along his scalp, a feeling of metal scraping over his scalp came to him as the memory of Jurin shaving his head resolved in his mind, that had been mere hours ago he thought, how had he forgotten that so soon after.

As he stood there, the Empress handed him a pile of clothes smiling at him. It took Rogan only a moment to realize he had been oblivious to the fact that he stood there naked before his Empress. Feeling the blood rush to his face, he turned bright red, snatching the bundle from the Empress Rogan ran for the small changing area in the corner of the room, the small partition the only private area available.

Once behind the paper partition, he breathed a sigh. “I’m so sorry my Empress, I had no idea, I mean I had forgotten I had been disrobed” he stammered and could hear the musical tones of her laughter.

“It’s fine Rogan, you have had an eventful day” she said dismissing the incident. Rogan quickly dressed into the robe and came out from behind the partition. She looked him over nodding approvingly as he stood there in similar robes to Vincent and the other Keepers.

“That looks right on you Rogan, now I can show you what we have done” she said and motioned for him to follow.

She led him out into the courtyard, Rogan looked up shielding his eyes as the sun came to rest above the ramparts, how long was I out he wondered following the Empress through the courtyard to a small area at the rear of the property.

The Empress pointed to a series of stones, varying in size laying a in a line in the middle of the open area, they started at the size of a ball that would fit into your palm and went up to one that was the size of a large knapsack.

Turning towards him, her expression relaxed but serious “Close your eyes, I want you to remember how it felt to use your power, I want you to reach out, don’t be alarmed, the runes will feel odd at first.”

Closing his eyes he reached out with his mind, feeling the crystals surrounding him, the hum of power a familiar companion to those who could wield it. Rogan began to pull energy into himself, unlike previously, the energy began to disseminate throughout his body, he felt the runes began to heat as the power coursed through them, the energy shaping itself to the spells now embedded over his entire being. He felt himself pulling more and more power to him, more than he had ever been able to do previously as the runes collected the energy, the newly acquired spells creating a reservoir. He smiled excitedly as he opened his eyes and looked to the Empress.

“I feel them, but it’s not a single thing, it feels like a swarm or a collective” he said trying to describe the feeling.

The Empress chuckled; Rogan couldn’t help but smile. “Yes, now, direct your will, lift the rock” she said, looking to the rocks, he sent his will, infusing it with the power now coursing through him at the smallest of the rocks, it was like nothing he had ever experienced.

The power shot out from his body, gathering up the stone and as he watched, the small rock, shot into the air, becoming so small he could no longer see it, as it launched itself into the clouds.

“Aurtus’ sword, that is incredible” he breathed. The Empress snapping her fingers to get his attention. “Be mindful of how much power you are gathering, feel the symbols, they will be warm, if you gather too much Rogan, it could cause Thalamic Burnout”.

He shot her a curious looking, he could feel the runes, they were warm “Thalamic Burnout?” he asked, and the Empress nodded solemnly. “You are moving energy, this creates heat, the more power you move the more heat is generated, understand if you generate too much it will raise the temperature of your body, the runes will burn and should your body grow too hot, you will do irreparable damage to your mind” she said and Rogan was quiet for a moment, she was serious, and her tone was grave. He nodded he would be mindful he thought.

Rogan gathered power once again, this time concentrating on the larger stone, he felt the power spread out to the runes, felt them heat up as the power coursed through them, his ability to gather large amounts of power exciting him, he directed it at the large rock, unleashing the massive energy at the massive stone, he watched as it too shot into the air, rising well up into the sky until once again he could no longer see it. The runes felt far warmer than before, the amount of power to move that larger stone, much more the that of the small one.

As he watched the stone reappeared beginning to grow as it fell back to the earth, after a moment it landed not far from where it had rested with a massive thud, the rock burying itself half into the soft earth.

“Good, you will have time to practice more before we set out” she said, and Rogan looked at her curiously “Set out?” he asked wondering where they were going. “Let me gather the others and you will find out.

Soon after nine men in robes which included Vincent, Jurin and himself gathered in the courtyard. Rogan could see they all had symbols covering their face, their heads all bald as the morning sun reflected off of them.

He turned forward to focus on his smiling Empress. “The day has come my knights, we prepare to leave, next week each of you will set out to your locations where you will eliminate the existing Seer, taking their place as my authority in this land we will begin to remove the useless political wrangling and Vicor will finally be ruled as one.

Once we have completed this and shown the people that those who rule are those with the power given to them by the gods themselves, we will begin to build our armies and this time next year we will bring The Kingdoms of Lusor and Dever to their knees, finally beginning our journey to bring this world under one rule, my rule.

To aid you in your jobs you each will take two of the wraiths as your bodyguards and enforcers. The Empress closed her eyes and a moment later twelve of the alabaster creatures came out into the sunlight, some on two legs and others moving on four. Rogan noticed the crystal in their head was glowing and as he looked between them and the Empress he finally understood.

The Empress was controlling them, and he studied the strange creatures in a new light. He could not believe he had doubted her even for a moment, he now felt the power of his gift, she had made him better, made him more powerful, not even his family would scoff at him now.

He would do his part to save humanity, whatever the price to his soul he resolved as two of the wraiths came to stand behind him.

No one would defy him, he would ensure that whichever territory he received would serve the Empress, either with pride or fear, they would serve her. And Rogan smiled,

the smile held malice and the promise of pain for those who stood against his Empress.
